beats.say: Windows XP's iconic Bliss wallpaper now appears on Crocs.
The Verge says Microsoft released limited edition XP-themed Crocs in 2025, priced at eighty dollars with a six-pack of Jibbitz charms including a Clippy shoe charm.
That photograph became the default desktop image for millions after XP launched in October 2001, yet mainstream support ended in 2009.
The Clippy paperclip returns as a shoe charm, turning the Office assistant into a collectible.
You can literally walk in a piece of computing history, blending twenty-five years of nostalgia into everyday footwear.
From desktop background to fashion statement, XP proves its cultural footprint never really left.

meta.summary: Windows XP's famous Bliss wallpaper appears on limited edition Crocs in 2025, complete with a Clippy shoe charm. The 2001 operating system's legacy extends from desktop backgrounds to fashion.
meta.comment: Would you wear Windows XP Crocs with a Clippy charm?
sources: The Verge, Microsoft's Windows XP Crocs are no joke, 2025-08-05
facts: Windows XP's default wallpaper is the Bliss image, a photograph of a landscape.
Microsoft created limited edition Windows XP-themed Crocs.
The Windows XP Crocs include a Clippy shoe charm.
The Crocs are priced at $80 and include a six-pack of Microsoft Jibbitz charms.
Windows XP was released to manufacturing on August 24, 2001, and later to retail on October 25 that year.
Mainstream support for Windows XP ended on April 14 2009 and extended support ended on April 8 2014.
